Define

$$
\rho_{\sigma}=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\frac{\alpha_n(\sigma)}{n!}\right)^{1/n},
$$

where $\alpha_n(\sigma)$ is the number of permutations in $\mathcal{S}_n$ avoiding $\sigma$ as a consecutive pattern. **Nakamura's least avoided pattern conjecture.** For any $\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_m$,

$$
\rho_{\sigma}\geq\rho_{(12\dots m-2,m,m-1)}.
$$

This identifies the pattern $(12\dots m-2,m,m-1)$ as the least avoided pattern according to the growth constant $\rho_\sigma$. $$

$$
F_n^*(x,y)=\prod_{k=1}^n\left(\sin\left(\frac{k\pi}{n}\right)x-\cos\left(\frac{k\pi}{n}\right)y\right).
$$

**Bean's conjecture.** The maximum value $M_n$ of $Q(F)$ over all such forms is attained precisely when $F$, up to multiplication by a complex number, is equivalent under $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb R)$ to $F_n^*$. Equivalently,

$$
M_n=Q(F_n^*).
$$

Moreover,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}M_n=2\pi.
$$

The quantity $Q(F)$ is invariant under multiplication by a complex number and under the action of $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb R)$, making this a natural extremal problem for binary forms.
